analyst_view.overall: Como arrive in outstanding form after a 9-1 Champions League win at Lens, having also scored four each against Leipzig and Manchester United in Europe. Inter lost the Milan derby, then beat Feyenoord in the Champions League midweek, and want a win before the international break. Two Italian previews leave Lautaro Martinez out of Inter's likely XI, with Pio Esposito and Thuram up front and Bastoni back from a European suspension; Cesc Fabregas looks set to pick his strongest Como side.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Como have been scoring heavily (22 in their last six by the site's own count, including the 9-1 in Lens), and Fabregas says they will come to San Siro to play their own game rather than sit deep. Inter, without Lautaro but with Thuram and Esposito, need a response after the derby, so an open game with a few goals seems more likely than a tight one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Both sides attack down the wings, with Dimarco and Spence pushing on for Inter and Da Cunha and Baturina wide for Como. Como keeping the ball more than most visitors could even out the corner count, so we stay near the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. Both teams want to play football and Fabregas called it a physically and mentally demanding game, but nothing in the news points to a bad-tempered match. We found nothing specific on Daniele Chiffi, so we stay with the low card count.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. Como's attack is in red-hot form, Inter will be pushing to bounce back from the derby, and both line up with two attacking wing-backs or full-backs. That points to plenty of shooting from both ends, so the total could come in above the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Como are creating and finishing chances at a rare rate (Douvikas, Nico Paz and Da Cunha all in form), and Inter's front two should test Butez often at home. We lean slightly above the site's number.
